cards.explanation: The answer is in the towns of Samaria. The king settled them there, and they took possession and lived in its towns (2 Kings 17:24). Five different places of origin, one region. I think that's a lot of new neighbors to get used to, friends.

The answer is that they didn't know what the God of the land requires. They told the king the peoples he had moved in did not know the requirements of the God of the land, and the lions were killing them off (2 Kings 17:26). Notice they're not blaming the weather or the neighborhood. They name the God of the land and what they don't know about Him. That's a real report, friends.

The king commands them to send back one of the priests they carried off from Samaria, to live there and teach (2 Kings 17:27). Think about that, friends. The king reaches back into the group he took away to find the teacher. Somebody's getting a very surprising travel notice.

The answer is False. The priest came and lived in Bethel, and he began to teach them how they should worship the LORD (2 Kings 17:28). Jerusalem isn't in this scene at all. I'd like to remind everybody that I got sent to a drawer, not a town, and I still found my way.

The answer is gods. The people of each nation kept making their own gods in the cities where they settled, even with a priest teaching them (2 Kings 17:29). That's not a small side project, friends. It's a heavy thing, and the text says it plainly.

The answer is in the shrines on the high places. They set up their gods in the shrines the people of Samaria had made (2 Kings 17:29). So they moved into places someone else had already built. Free real estate, wrong use of it, friends.

The answer is priests of all sorts. The new residents worshiped the LORD, but they also appointed for themselves priests of all sorts to serve in the shrines of the high places (2 Kings 17:32). Not one priest. All sorts. That's like getting a whole bakery's worth of bakers without ever checking who's in charge of the oven.

The answer is customs. They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods according to the customs of the nations from which they had been carried away (2 Kings 17:33). They kept the old habits from back home. I've kept habits too long myself, friends, and mine were just about cookie sizes.

The first command is, do not worship other gods. The LORD commanded the Israelites, "Do not worship other gods or bow down to them; do not serve them or sacrifice to them." (2 Kings 17:35). Notice how that one line covers worship, bowing, serving and sacrificing, friends. It's the very thing the settlers were doing in the shrines.

The answer is True. The LORD told them, "You are to bow down to Him and offer sacrifices to Him." (2 Kings 17:36). That comes right after reminding them He brought them out of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm. Who rescued them and who they bow to go together, friends.

The promise is that He will deliver them from all their enemies. The LORD says to worship the LORD their God, "…and He will deliver you from the hands of all your enemies." (2 Kings 17:39). Look at the pairing, friends. First He says to worship Him alone, then He tells them what He'll do. That's a promise worth holding onto.

The answer is False. The nations worshiped the LORD but also served their idols, and to this day their children and grandchildren continue to do as their fathers did (2 Kings 17:41). The habit rolled right down the family line, friends. It's easier to hand down a recipe than a change of heart.
